<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# I'm currently at SkyBlue_1 (col 22). Let me test what UP does.
# First, record current state of SkyBlue_1

top_patterns_dict = {
    0: "BBBBB\nB...B\nBB.BB\nB...B\nB...B",
    1: "BBBB.\nB..BB\nB...B\nBB..B\n.BBBB",
    2: "B...B\nBBBBB\n..B..\nBBBBB\nB...B",
    3: "BBBB.\nB..B.\nB..BB\nB..B.\nBBBB.",
    4: "....B\n..B.B\nBBBBB\n..B.B\n....B",
    5: "BBBBB\nB..B.\nB..B.\nBBBB.\nB....",
    6: "..B..\nBBBBB\nB.B.B\nB.B.B\n..B..",
    7: "..BBB\n..B.B\nBBBBB\nB.B..\nBBB..",
    8: "....B\n..B.B\nBBBBB\nB.B..\nB....",
    9: "BBBBB\nB...B\nB.BBB\nB.B.B\nBBBBB",
    10: "BB.BB\nB...B\nB...B\nBBBBB\nB...B",
    11: "..B..\nBBBBB\nB.B.B\nBBBBB\n..B..",
}

def get_pattern(r, c):
    ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
    pat = ""
    for dr in range(1, 6):
        row_str = ""
        for dc in range(1, 6):
            ch = ascii_lines[r + dr][c + dc]
            row_str += "B" if ch == "B" else "."
        pat += row_str + "\n"
    return pat.strip()

def find_match(pat):
    for idx, tpat in top_patterns_dict.items():
        if pat == tpat:
            return idx
    return -1

# Current SkyBlue_1 state
skyblue1_before = get_pattern(40, 21)
match_before = find_match(skyblue1_before)
print(f"SkyBlue_1 before UP: Cell {match_before}")

# Do UP and check what changes
action(['UP'])

# Check cursor position after UP
seg = current_frame.segmentation
white_objects = []
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'W':
        boundary = n['boundary']
        min_row = min(p[0] for p in boundary)
        min_col = min(p[1] for p in boundary)
        white_objects.append((min_row, min_col))

print(f"After UP, white objects at: {white_objects}")

# Check SkyBlue_1 state after UP
skyblue1_after = get_pattern(40, 21)
match_after = find_match(skyblue1_after)
print(f"SkyBlue_1 after UP: Cell {match_after}")

# Check if SkyBlue_1 changed
print(f"SkyBlue_1 changed: {skyblue1_before != skyblue1_after}")

# Also check Pink_1 state (in case UP moved cursor to Pink row)
pink1_after = get_pattern(51, 21)
print(f"Pink_1 after UP: {find_match(pink1_after)}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
